precepts.text: A man in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, with light and understanding and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods, made master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans and soothsayers, a dissolver of doubts; Daniel was set over the elite brain of Babylon.
precepts.point: It is no coincidence that Babylon used Daniel to advance itself and modern Babylon used a black man to lay out its capital; the slave masters knew that though captive we were not stupid, and Egypt, Persia, Greece, Rome and America all used the genius of the conquered.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Years later, Belshazzar needed a vision explained, and he was told: “There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of thy father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him.” Daniel had the wisdom of the gods.

Nebuchadnezzar “made master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers” this man. The Chaldeans were the elite brain of Babylon, the wisest men in the kingdom, and Daniel was set over them, and over the witches and sorcerers too. Read on: “an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel.” He was a dissolver of doubts: any doubt you had, he could dissolve it.

“now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.” Go get Daniel; if anyone knows, it's Daniel. By then he was older, and the captive of Judah was still the wisest man in Babylon. That is the superiority of the chosen people, and the reason the nations have always used the genius of Israel.

precepts.text: Even before the captivity we were warned we would see these gods of silver and gold in Babylon and told not to fear or worship them.
precepts.point: This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel. They drank and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone.

note.label: Daniel 5: The Handwriting on the Wall

precepts.why:
Before the captivity, Israel was warned what they would see in Babylon: “So when ye be come unto Babylon, ye shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence. Now shall ye see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.” Those are the very gods Belshazzar and his thousand lords praised as they drank: “the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.”

The warning was not to fear them or worship them: “Beware therefore that ye in no wise be like to strangers, neither be ye and of them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them. But say ye in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee.”

Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel, took the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar carried out of the temple in Jerusalem, and he, his princes, his wives, and his concubines drank wine in them and praised the gods of gold and silver. The multitude in Babylon worshipped those gods; Israel was told beforehand to say in their hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee.

precepts.text: The gods of silver and gold cannot save themselves, so we were warned not to fear them.
precepts.point: Belshazzar had not humbled his heart though he knew all this, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from the temple vessels, and praised gods of silver, gold, brass, iron, wood, and stone that see not nor hear, while the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify.

note.label: Daniel 5: The Handwriting on the Wall

precepts.why:
Daniel told Belshazzar he had “praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know”. Baruch had already said the same of them: “Yet cannot these gods save themselves from rust and moth, though they be covered with purple raiment. They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them.” A god that cannot keep the dust off its own face, that rusts and is eaten by moth under its purple raiment, is no god.

“And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as though he were a judge of the country. He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an axe: but cannot deliver himself from war and thieves. Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not.” They hold a sceptre, a dagger and an axe, and cannot save themselves; so we were warned not to fear them.

That is what makes Belshazzar's sin so plain. He knew all that had happened to his father Nebuchadnezzar, how the Most High gave him the kingdom, deposed him when his heart was lifted up in pride, and drove him to dwell with the wild asses till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men; and still he did not humble his heart. He lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven, drank from the vessels of his house, and praised gods that cannot save themselves, while “the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified”.

note.label: THE ART OF A DYNAMIC TEACHER

precepts.why: What was that wisdom of the gods? “For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit”: it will not stay with you if you are deceitful. “And remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” Who will not abide? The Father and his Son. They are the spirit of discipline that resides in us when we do the commandments and keep the sayings.

note.label: THE ART OF A DYNAMIC TEACHER

precepts.why:
When you acquire this spirit, what spirit should you not have? “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power”: there's that word again. “And of love”: keeping commandments. “And of a sound mind.” All of those amount to one word: fortitude. Not fear, fortitude, and a readiness of mind.

As this truth progresses and people take notice of us, some Israelites will get fearful and turn into Christians and podcast prophets. After the Jersey shooting, when Muslims shot up a Jewish market and tried to blame us, some groups stopped wearing their fringes so they would not be associated. Now a camp leader complains that Israelites marched on a Christian event: leave them alone, they believe in Christ, go march on the Arabs. Which Christ do they believe in? These men lack fortitude. They have other nations in their camp and teach that the nations will be saved, and that emboldens them to speak against us. Make a decision; the Most High is going to separate the men from the boys.

“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That is the stipulation for getting the spirit, the Holy Spirit. “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth.” So the holy spirit is the spirit of truth; that’s what the Babylonians called the spirit of the holy gods in Daniel 5.

“Whom the world cannot receive”: the world can’t receive the Holy Spirit, “because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him.” Y’all be looking at these people on TV that claim to have the Holy Spirit, but they don’t keep no commandments; they don’t have the Holy Spirit. All that rolling, I’m slain in the spirit, rolling on the floor foaming at the mouth: that’s not the Holy Spirit. That’s a fornicating demon. Foaming at the mouth, doing back flips in church: the hell is this?

“But ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you”: he’s telling you who the holy spirit is. Verse 18 seals the deal, and you have to stress the right word: “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He’s telling you he’s the holy spirit. It’s not Elijah Muhammad, it’s not Dr York, it’s not Muhammad. Christ is telling you, I am the Holy Spirit, I will come to you. I don’t see how people could be so damn dumb.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.” When you receive the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit, number one, the stipulation is you must be keeping the commandments (verse 15). Then he shall teach you all things, “and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

So the Holy Spirit would teach us about the speakings and sayings of Christ: how the Israelites would fall and go into captivity, and then be resurrected in the last days and wake up again. How come no church that claims to have the Holy Spirit knows that? They don’t know it, because you got to keep the commandments. A preacher on TV waves his dirty jacket, a jacket that cost probably $2,000, and people fall out and say I’m slain in the spirit. The hell is this? He don’t do it in the hospital.

Verse 23 is the point. “How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity?” Reading all those stupid books by that guy Carson: you simple for that. “And the scorners delight in their scorning”: there’s no God, there’s no Christ; they delight in scorning. “And fools hate knowledge”: fools hate God’s laws.

“Turn you at my reproof”: God’s reproof is his laws, so turn you at my reproof means keep God’s laws. And what will God do for us if we turn at his reproof? “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” That’s John 14:15, the same thing Christ said: keep my commandments and I will pray the Father, and you shall receive the Holy Spirit. Turn at my reproof and I will pour out my spirit unto you. It’s saying the same thing; that is the spirit that was in Daniel.

Daniel saw dreams and was able to interpret things, and the scriptures talk about that in these last days. When you read Joel 2, do not start at verse 28; always start at verse 27. Christians don’t like that, because they like to make Joel 2:28 all inclusive, for all races of people, but it’s not talking about all races of people.

“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” Christians hate that verse. So you mean he’s not the god of the Chinese? No. He’s not the god of the white man? No. Not the god of the Arabs? No. He’s nobody else’s God but our God. “And my people shall never be ashamed.”

“I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh”: Christians highlight all flesh and say see, everybody. No, dummy, verse 27 already cleared the thought: it’s talking about the Israelites. That spirit is the same spirit Daniel had, the same spirit Christ was talking about, the same spirit we rolling in. “And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: And also upon the servants”: some brothers and sisters had servants and will have servants; you have employees, workers. “And upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit”: that’s the Holy Spirit.

Although this occurred in the book of Acts chapter two, from verse 30 down is really talking about these last days. “And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke”: destruction. “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” So before the second coming the Lord said, I’m going to pour out my spirit upon all flesh, meaning all the flesh of the Israelites.

“Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered”, and here’s the answer: “for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance.” Deliverance is not for all races on the planet earth. “And in the remnant whom the Lord shall call”: that’s still Israel. We all want that Holy Spirit; we want the Lord to pour his spirit out upon us.

Remember what Christ said: “Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” So when we come into this truth we are the light. We have that spirit; the spirit of the holy God is on us, and we are that light of the world, the same light and understanding that was found in Daniel.

“But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated”: that is the same illumination as what Daniel had. “Ye endured a great fight of afflictions”: so we must endure a great fight of afflictions soon to come.

“But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?” You can’t compare a man or a woman who is holding the illumination of the Lord, who has the love of the Lord on them.

“Turn thee, O Jacob”: we are Jacob. “And take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.” That is the light and understanding that was found in Daniel, held out to Jacob.

Herod did the same thing. “Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon”: that’s in Lebanon. They “desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king’s country”: there was a huge trade of imports and exports of food between Herod’s kingdom and Tyre and Sidon.

“Upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them”: he gave a great BS speech. “And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.” Watch this: “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him”. Why? “Because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” See that: pride, pride, pride. Just like Nebuchadnezzar.

This is where it was told to Nebuchadnezzar: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”. Man does not want to acknowledge that the Most High rules this planet. Man wants to think he does things of his own accord; that’s called pride.

“And giveth it to whomsoever he will”: God gives the kingdom to whomsoever he will. “And setteth up over it the basest of men.” Base is the root word of basement: the bottom level, the lowest you can go. So God said, I set the lowest of the nations over this world. You think the white man is so high and mighty; God says no, those are base people. A people who create a weapon to destroy themselves, a base people. A people who create fake food to kill the population, a base people.

Your life was lent to you. “He maketh a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returneth to the same”: you return back to the earth out of which you were taken, “when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.”

Our lives are not our own. The life we’re living now was loaned to us, lent to us. You think you’re alive because your mama had you? No: the fact that you’re breathing, that’s a loan; God is lending you that. And it’s going to be demanded: that breath you’re taking right now will be demanded one day. We must all acknowledge that. That is the God in whose hand thy breath is, whom Belshazzar did not glorify.

This goes for all of us, because many brothers and sisters do this. “Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow.” We don’t know what tomorrow is going to bring. “For what is your life? It is even a vapour”: it’s a smoke, “that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.” Here today, gone tomorrow.

“For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.” That’s what we got to start saying. Not, hey, tomorrow I’m going to do this, I’m going to do that. No, that’s pride: you don’t know that God’s going to give you that life tomorrow.

“But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.” James is saying it’s evil when you say what you’re going to do tomorrow, and your life is not even your own. “Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” If you know the right things to say and you choose not to say them, it is sin to you.

That’s something we often slip with the tongue. We got to catch ourselves and say, Lord’s will, if life lasts and the Lord allows me, I’ll do this, that and the other. We must always give God the glory.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified. He did not glorify the God of heaven even though he knew what happened to his father.

Nebuchadnezzar, when Daniel gave him the dream about him being the head of gold, got lifted up in his mind and set himself up as a god, and the Lord jacked him up. He was cast down, running around crazy in the woods. The Lord was saying, do not exalt yourself, I am the one that lifts people up and takes them down. So his son knew that, and yet his son still tested the Lord.

points: “Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel.” When Daniel and the prophets spoke there was no I agree, I disagree, that's your opinion. They dissolved all doubts. What the Bible says is what it means; there is no you have your Bible version. You're just wrong, and it's okay to be wrong. “Now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.”

note.label: THE ART OF A DYNAMIC TEACHER

points: Nebuchadnezzar was in power, then he died, and some time later his grandson took over. “Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.” He commanded to bring “the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem”; next to the word father there is a note that says grandfather.

They brought the golden vessels of the house of God, and the king, his princes, his wives and his concubines “drank in them.” They were mocking the vessels that were stolen from the temple of the Lord. “They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.”

“In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.” He saw the hand writing on the wall. “Then the king’s countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed”: he got real scared. “And his knees smote one against another”: that’s great fear. When you see a hand appear out of nowhere and just start writing on the walls, what the hell is this? He’s terrified.

He cried aloud for “the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers”, promising that whoever could read the writing should be clothed with scarlet, have a chain of gold about his neck, “and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.” Then came in all the king’s wise men, and none of the astrologers could interpret the writing on the wall. Y’all can read the rest on your own; the children have read this already in Sabbath class.

“There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods”: there’s a man in your kingdom, Belshazzar, who has the spirit of the holy gods. “Light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him”: all that we read in chapter one. Nebuchadnezzar made him master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans and soothsayers.

“Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts”: when Daniel spoke, that is what they were making reference to. He dissolved all doubts; he was a dissolver of doubts when he spoke. “Now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.”

Now they call Daniel. Remember Daniel is old now; they were 70 years in Babylon, so he’s up in age. “Art thou that Daniel, which art of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Jewry?”

“I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.” See what it says in verse 14, the spirit of the gods is in thee, and remember verse 11, a man in whom is “the spirit of the holy gods.” What they’re making reference to is what the scriptures call the Holy Spirit, what the Hebrew community calls the ruach. The holy spirit is the spirit of truth; that’s what the Babylonians called the spirit of the holy gods.

We all want that Holy Spirit; we want the Lord to pour His Spirit out upon us. Here they are having a conversation with Daniel, and he’s an old man now. “I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.” See that light and understanding there.
That same spirit that was on Daniel is to be on us.

“But they could not shew the interpretation of the thing”, because the writing was in ancient Hebrew. It wasn’t Aramaic; it was in the pure tongue they call the king’s tongue, the king’s language, which was the ancient Hebrew.

“And I have heard of thee, that thou canst make interpretations, and dissolve doubts”. Remember when Daniel came, they had to teach him a new language; in chapter one it says they had to teach him their language. So nobody knew his language.
“Let thy gifts be to thyself”: keep your gifts, I don’t need your gifts. “And give thy rewards to another”: give your rewards to somebody else.
“O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour”. Now he’s reading the writing: he’s looking at the wall as he’s talking.
“All people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him”: he conquered everybody.

“But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride”. In what? In pride. King Nebuchadnezzar had great pride, and he parted from the one true God. Daniel was trying to teach him and show him about the Living God, and he said, I don’t want to hear that.

“Till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men”: he had to acknowledge the one true God. “And that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.” Nebuchadnezzar had to realize what Daniel was trying to show him: you are only ruling because the one true God allowed you to rule. In his mind, his pride said no, I’m ruling because I’m all powerful.
“And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this”: he didn’t humble his heart though he knew all that Daniel just said. He didn’t humble himself.
“They have brought the vessels of his house before thee”: they brought the vessels of the house of the Lord in mockery. While Daniel is talking he’s looking at the ancient Hebrew writing on the wall.
“And the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified”. That’s why we went to Wisdom of Solomon: our breath is in God’s hand.
“MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.” They fell around 529; that’s when the Medes and Persians came in and destroyed Babylon.
“TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting”: found lacking.
“Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.” That is what Daniel was speaking of: the Persians and Medes were going to come and destroy the kingdom.
“In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain”: he was killed, murdered, slain.
“And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old”: 62.
We got to make sure that we don’t have that spirit of pride in us. Always, in all things, acknowledge the one true God.
